mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive months of >1% INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above their respective 12-month averages signals a monetary policy tightening in an inflationary environment, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed their 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) signals robust household demand and construction activity, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth and HOUST both rise in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS and HOUST both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation, prompting preemptive monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 3.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of the economic regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines by more than 0.5% for three consecutive months.
